title: Automating construction contract review using knowledge graph-enhanced large language models
task: 知识图增强的施工合同自动审查与风险识别
inputData: 施工合同文本 + Nested Contract Knowledge Graph (NCKG) + 风险本体
contribution: 提出Nested Contract Knowledge Graph，以RDF-star表达合同中的嵌套语义关系，并将图相似检索、结构化查询和LLM知识增强提示结合为GraphRAG合同审查流程，提高复杂合同风险分析的准确性与可解释性。
abstract: This study integrates a Nested Contract Knowledge Graph with LLM reasoning for automated construction contract review. The NCKG models fine-grained and nested contract semantics using a dedicated ontology and RDF-star, while GraphRAG retrieves structured knowledge to ground risk analysis. The tuning-free method is evaluated on international EPC contracts against LLM-only and vector-database-enhanced baselines.
methodology: The framework contains two major components. Domain NCKG development constructs a semantic contract graph from standard forms using LLM-assisted extraction followed by manual verification; the graph contains an ontology layer and a nested knowledge-representation layer implemented with RDF-star. NCKG-enhanced review then combines graph similarity search and structured graph queries to retrieve relevant entities, events and constraints before knowledge-enhanced LLM reasoning. The experiments compare LLM-only prompting, conventional vector-database retrieval and NCKG-enhanced retrieval on construction contract risk clauses from international project forms.
results: Experimental evaluation shows that NCKG-enhanced review outperforms both LLM-only and vector-database-enhanced baselines in knowledge retrieval and risk-review accuracy while producing more interpretable risk summaries. The study demonstrates that explicit nested graph semantics are particularly useful when risks depend on relations within and across clauses rather than isolated sentence similarity.
taskEn: Knowledge-graph-enhanced automated construction contract review and risk identification
inputDataEn: Construction contract text plus a Nested Contract Knowledge Graph (NCKG) and risk ontology
operationEvidence: GraphRAG retrieves NCKG entities, nested relations, and constraints through similarity/structured queries and grounds LLM-based contract risk analysis.
relationshipNote: Distinct follow-on study from the same research line: this paper replaces the earlier vectorized natural-language knowledge base with an RDF-star Nested Contract Knowledge Graph and GraphRAG evaluation.
